description: HTML conformance fixture for the parseHtml capability. Each case is what a style returns as `content`, plus the RichText the core must derive from it. The allowed tags/attributes below are the whole cross-host surface: a host whose parser handles them identically renders the same output. Cases marked `caveat` pin behaviour that differs between HTML parsers (Gecko in a Zotero host, linkedom in the testkit) — they are recorded so a divergence is noticed, not assumed away.

tags.sc: small-caps: the text itself is rewritten into small-cap glyphs (no mark survives)
tags.a: link mark when href is http:, https:, doi: or a well-formed banyan://entry/<id>
tags.span: color / background-color from style; the nocase class suppresses text-case
tags.br: a newline in the text (not a mark)

allowed.ignoredTags: any tag outside `tags` neither opens markup parsing nor produces a mark
allowed.markupDetection: content that contains none of the listed tags is treated as plain text and only the entities & < > " '   are decoded

cases.name: illegal-nesting
cases.caveat: The parser repairs the crossed tags: the italic run ends with the bold run, and the trailing 'italic' is plain. A different HTML parser may repair it differently; a Zotero host and the testkit are expected to agree because both hand the same DOM shape to the core.

cases.name: unknown-tag
cases.caveat: `<u>` is not in the allowed tag list, so the content never enters markup parsing and stays literal text.

cases.name: script-content
cases.caveat: Script text is walked as a text node: it is never executed (the style context has no DOM or globals) but it does appear in the output.

cases.name: span-background
cases.caveat: `background-color` yields only the background mark; a Zotero host sees the same DOM attribute and therefore the same result.

cases.name: small-caps
cases.caveat: `<sc>` is baked into small-cap code points by the core, so the mark does not survive and the renderer emits plain text.

cases.name: nbsp-in-markup
cases.caveat: Inside markup the HTML parser decodes ` ` to U+00A0; the plain-text path does the same.

cases.name: entity-out-of-range
cases.caveat: A code point outside the Unicode range stays literal text; the core never emits a replacement character.

cases.name: pseudo-tag-is-text
cases.caveat: A start tag without a closing tag is not treated as markup, so prose containing `<` and `>` survives verbatim.
